name: aim3-integration
title: Aim 3 — Compartment-Coupled Integration
description:
Aim 3 is the integration layer and the core software deliverable of MOSAIC. It connects the vaginal and gut–liver models from Aims 1 and 2 to explicitly simulate the synthesis, microbial deconjugation, enterohepatic recycling, and systemic transport of sex hormones across biological compartments. The central design principle is that each component model keeps its own assumptions, units, and biological scope; MOSAIC supplies executable interfaces (built on Vivarium / process-bigraph) that let one model's outputs serve as another's inputs or constraints — metabolite exchange, hormone production and recycling, growth rates, community composition, and agent behavior.

This investigation hosts the seam itself: the shared hormone store, the typed interfaces between GEM / community / PKPD / agent-based Processes, and the system-level studies that test whether perturbations propagate correctly across compartments.
biological_story: Hormone homeostasis is the thread that ties MOSAIC together. The gut microbiome contributes to systemic estrogen availability through microbial deconjugation and enterohepatic recycling; estrogen in turn modulates hepatic metabolism, immune responses, and vaginal epithelial physiology. A perturbation in one compartment — a shift in gut community composition, a change in reproductive stage, a drug — can therefore ripple outward to the others. Aim 3 makes that ripple executable: a shared hormone state couples the vaginal, gut, and liver models so that outputs from one become constraints on the next. The deliverable is the first human-relevant in silico platform that treats hormone homeostasis as a dynamic, system-level regulator of host–microbiome metabolic interactions.
question: When the Aim 1 (vaginal/BV) and Aim 2 (gut–liver/MASLD) models are coupled through explicit hormone synthesis, microbial deconjugation, enterohepatic recycling, and systemic transport of sex hormones, do systemic variations in microbiome composition and endocrine status propagate across organ systems to alter downstream metabolic network behavior and patient-specific therapeutic response?
hypothesis: Explicit mechanistic interfaces between disparate modeling paradigms — the process-bigraph seam — let the independently developed Aim 1 and Aim 2 models function as a single integrated representation of hormone-regulated human physiology, with hormone homeostasis as the coupling mechanism that carries compartment-level perturbations system-wide.

executive.what_is_this: Aim 3 of MOSAIC — the planned integration seam that couples the Aim 1 and Aim 2 models through hormone homeostasis to simulate system-level feedback and hormone-mediated transport.
executive.verdict: Planned — depends on Aim 1 and Aim 2 components; seam not yet built.

decisions_needed.question: What is the shared hormone-state interface contract?
decisions_needed.context: Defines the typed store (species, units, local vs. global pools) that every model reads/writes — the backbone of the seam.

decisions_needed.question: How is enterohepatic recycling represented across the gut–liver seam?
decisions_needed.context: Microbial deconjugation + reabsorption is the mechanism linking gut community output to systemic estrogen.

scientific_argument.main_claim: Explicit, executable interfaces between independently developed models — coupled through hormone homeostasis — yield an integrated representation of hormone-regulated physiology in which perturbations propagate across compartments.
evidence_for: Vivarium / process-bigraph already composes heterogeneous simulators as typed, reusable modules across scales.
Hormone homeostasis (estrogen metabolism + enterohepatic recycling) is a plausible, well-motivated coupling variable linking gut, liver, and vaginal compartments.
evidence_against: Differences in spatial/temporal scale at the interfaces between paradigms can make input/output relationships hard to identify.
Integrated prediction failures may be hard to localize to a single component.
caveats: If interface dynamics prove intractable, a fallback is to abstract some connections with learned (e.g. graph neural network) surrogates while keeping components mechanistic.
Integration is gated on Aim 1 and Aim 2 reaching usable component models.
